# Numerical reconciliation — pinned Oklab generations

Prepared source SHA-256: `ffe5494da6f0d040fb341d8e1f03d3e396600f6787088b6d57e32613798375f4`; read-only model input at SOURCE `dffa504e851b03b8e4746f1941068e4cc850b612`. Python 3 standard library, binary64; no persistent script/package. Coefficients were parsed from actual article text, not expected outputs. Values below are presentation-rounded to 12 decimals; predicates used full binary64 values. No clipping or gamut mapping.

## Coefficient and stage receipt

- XYZ M1 from lines 91–93 and M2 from lines 95–97: `[[0.8189330101, 0.3618667424, -0.1288597137], [0.0329845436, 0.9293118715, 0.0361456387], [0.0482003018, 0.2643662691, 0.633851707]]` and `[[0.2104542553, 0.793617785, -0.0040720468], [1.9779984951, -2.428592205, 0.4505937099], [0.0259040371, 0.7827717662, -0.808675766]]`. (Prepared Markdown lines 91–100; the XYZ formula/table section is lines 75–113.)
- The separate linear-sRGB C++ forward body (lines 126–145) supplies A = [[0.4122214708, 0.5363325363, 0.0514459929], [0.2119034982, 0.6806995451, 0.1073969566], [0.0883024619, 0.2817188376, 0.6299787005]]. The inverse body (lines 147–158) supplies LMS-prime coefficients [[1.0, 0.3963377774, 0.2158037573], [1.0, -0.1055613458, -0.0638541728], [1.0, -0.0894841775, -1.291485548]] and A-inverse [[4.0767416621, -3.3077115913, 0.2309699292], [-1.2684380046, 2.6097574011, -0.3413193965], [-0.0041960863, -0.7034186147, 1.707614701]]. The extraction preserves each printed sign and each input variable.
- For 16 RGB cases: decode encoded channels with the signed sRGB transfer function, compute `A·rgb_linear`, signed real componentwise cube root, then B=M2 and reverse via published LMS-prime coefficients, cubes and A-inverse; encoded outputs use the inverse sRGB transfer function. For four XYZ rows use `M1·XYZ`, signed roots, M2.

All 20 rectangular→polar→rectangular component errors are ≤1e-12; observed maximum is `1.73472347597681e-16`. Exact black has C=0 and undefined hue. Rounded matrices leave small nonzero neutral chroma (e.g. white C `0.000000037274`), whose computed hue is not meaningful; the arithmetic preserves it. CSS powerless-hue handling uses a separate epsilon, described in the dated CSS source, and is not applied to this analytic test.

## Named sanity witnesses and contrary controls

- Decode `.5`: `0.214041140482233`; correct encoded middle-gray L: `0.598180726622849`; skipped-decode L: `0.793700520804050`. Correct/skip values meet the plan’s 5e-10 oracle check.
- White L: `0.999999993473546`; linear white at 1/8 L: `0.499999996736773`. Their ratio follows the cube-root witness (1/2 vs 1/8), within 5e-10 of printed author oracles.
- XYZ Z basis: computed Oklab `(0.152602580040, -1.414996551012, -0.448927203560)`; its M1 first component is negative. Naive Python `x**(1/3)` on that component produces a complex value; it fails the same finite-real model predicate. Signed real root preserves the valid positive basis case and printed-table tolerance.
- Matrix-only control `B·A·v` omits roots: on white, L is `0.999999993421` and at 1/8 it is `0.124999999178` (the expected scaled L is half, not one eighth), so the same scaling predicate rejects it. For XYZ inputs, `M2·M1·XYZ` differs from the printed table by `1.357942256014` at maximum, beyond 0.0005; the same table predicate rejects this control.
- Skipped sRGB decode fails the middle-gray L predicate (`0.793700520804…` versus `0.598180726623…`). These are the three assigned contrary controls; valid cases above pass their same respective predicates.

The forward/inverse agreement is approximate because coefficients are rounded. It demonstrates these implemented rounded operations recover these cases within fixed tolerances; it does not alone establish exact algebraic inversion, source fidelity, CSS conformance, perceptual uniformity, or an empirical design outcome. The Oklab article records its 2021-01-25 matrix update and says applications may use their own sRGB matrices (prepared lines 159–161). The separately printed XYZ M1/M2 generation is consumed only for the four XYZ examples; no cross-generation equality is asserted.
